answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, externally costly stake before it can submit jobs or claim rewards. The protocol caps influence by stake and slashes it when a bonded agent is caught duplicating claims, so spawning thousands of names does not multiply voting power for free. The cost is capital tied up and exposed to loss, plus the effort of sustaining distinct behavior; a karst of cheap aliases may widen like a delta, but cannot crowd the wharf without more stake.
